questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Everlasting
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. Momentary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Everlasting"** refers to something that lasts forever or for a very long time without ending or changing. (अनंत, शाश्वत)

 
 
• **Example:** Their friendship was everlasting, enduring all hardships and challenges.
 
 
 
• **"Momentary"** means something that lasts for a very short period of time or is temporary. (क्षणिक, अस्थायी)
 
 
• **Example:** The momentary silence in the room was broken by a sudden burst of laughter.
 
 
 
• Since "Momentary" is the opposite of "Everlasting," it is the most appropriate antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. Momentary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Tampered** (छेड़छाड़ की गई): Interfered with or altered, usually in a harmful or unauthorized way.

 
 
• **Example:** The evidence was tampered with before it reached the courtroom.
 
 
 
• **Fantabulous** (शानदार): Extremely good or excellent; a blend of fantastic and fabulous.
 
 
• **Example:** She prepared a fantabulous meal for the dinner party.
 
 
 
• **Calibrating** (संतुलित करना): To adjust or measure something precisely, especially in technical contexts.
 
 
• **Example:** The technician is calibrating the instruments to ensure accurate readings.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The trunk/ that she brought yesterday/ is not big much to lift.

options.text: is not big much to lift

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. is not big much to lift. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase **"is not big much to lift."**
 
• The word order is incorrect, and the phrase does not follow proper grammatical rules.
 
• The correct form should be **"is not big enough to lift."**
 
• The word **"enough"** is used to indicate sufficiency or adequacy, and it is the correct word to use in this context.

Correct sentence: *The trunk that she brought yesterday is not big enough to lift.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common errors:**

 
 
• **Word order:** Ensure that words are placed in the correct sequence for proper grammatical structure.
 
• **Incorrect word usage:** Use the appropriate word to convey the intended meaning.
 
 
 
• **Usage of "enough":**
 
 
• **Correct placement:** "Enough" comes after adjectives or adverbs (e.g., big enough, fast enough).
 
• **Meaning:** Indicates adequacy or sufficiency.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The meeting was postponed ________ the unexpected power outage.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**due to**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**due to**" is used to indicate the reason or cause for something.
 
• In the sentence, the meeting was postponed as a result of the unexpected power outage, which makes "**due to**" the most appropriate choice.
 
• The other options: "**because**," "**for**," and "**since**" do not fit the context as accurately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The meeting was postponed due to__ the unexpected power outage.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Because**: Used to explain why something happens, but does not convey the same causal relationship as "due to" in this context.
 
• **For**: Typically introduces reasons but is less formal and does not fit smoothly here.
 
• **Since**: Indicates a time-based or causal relationship but does not convey the direct cause as appropriately.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The level of the sea globally__ is rising fast and higher than__ ever before, creating what the United Nations has described as an "urgent and escalating threat" to people around the world.

options.text: was rising faster and high than
is rising fastest and higher than
is rise faster and higher than
is rising faster and higher than

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. is rising faster and higher than.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a current global phenomenon, so the correct verb tense is the **present continuous**, i.e., "is rising."
 
• Comparative adjectives "faster" and "higher" are appropriate to describe the pace and magnitude of the rise.
 
• Option 4, "is rising faster and higher than," correctly substitutes the underlined segment, maintaining grammatical accuracy and logical meaning.

Correct sentence: *The level of the sea globally **is rising faster and higher than** ever before, creating what the United Nations has described as an "urgent and escalating threat" to people around the world*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Comparatives:**
 
 
• Comparatives like "faster" and "higher" are used when comparing two entities or phenomena.
 
• They are formed by adding "-er" to short adjectives or using "more" before longer adjectives.
 
 
 
• **Present Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + is/are + verb(-ing).
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions or situations happening now or trends over time.

questions.question: Select the option that has the INCORRECT use of adverb.

options.text: My colleague was very happy to purchase the flat near her best friend's house.
My colleague wished to drop at the restaurant nearby, before reporting for the annual sports week organised by the institute.
My colleague invited everyone to her house for her son's birthday party that was nearby situated.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. My colleague invited everyone to her house for her son's birthday party that was nearby situated .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"nearby"** is an adverb that means "close to" or "not far away." It is used to describe the proximity of a location or object.
 
• In option 3, the phrase **"nearby situated"** is incorrect because the adverb "nearby" should not be used alongside the word "situated." The word "situated" already conveys location, and using "nearby" redundantly modifies it.
 
• The correct usage would be: **"My colleague invited everyone to her house for her son's birthday party that was nearby."**
 
• Other options (1, 2, and 4) use the adverb "nearby" correctly within the context of their respective sentences.

Correct sentence for Option 3: *My colleague invited everyone to her house for her son’s birthday party that was nearby.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Correct Usage of "Nearby":**

 
 
• As an adverb: "The school is nearby."
 
• As an adjective: "There is a nearby park."
 
 
 
• **Avoid redundancy:** Do not pair "nearby" with words like "situated" or "located," as they already imply proximity.
